(a) Except as otherwise provided herein, it shall be unlawful for any person to consume any spirituous, malt or alcoholic beverage of any kind in or upon any street, alley, sidewalk or other public way or place within the city, or to possess or consume any alcoholic beverage within any public building, except that such beverages may be possessed and consumed, in strict accordance with all applicable laws, ordinances, rules and regulations within, and only within, the premises, as that term is defined at section 6-51 of this Code, of any licensed establishment located within any public building.
(b) From time to time and within its sole discretion, as set out herein, city council may permit the sale and/or consumption of alcoholic beverages, including beer, wine and spiritous liquors, only at public or quasi public events in the city. Such sale and/or consumption shall be permitted only at such events as shall be authorized by council and for which a permit has been issued by the clerk. Such permits shall be inscribed by the city clerk with the location, effective date or dates of such permits, the event or events covered by such permit, the type and quantity of alcoholic beverages which may be served, the person or persons so authorized to serve such beverages, and any other conditions deemed desirable by city council.
(c) Any person desiring to apply to council for any such permit shall do so by making a written application at least seven days in advance, which application shall include the following information:
(1) The name and address of the person responsible for the staging of the purposed event, including other relevant information on any organization which proposes to sponsor such event;
(2) The specific location of the event;
(3) A description of the event, including the public or quasi public nature of the event. The date and time or times of such proposed event;
(4) The nature and quantity of all alcoholic beverages proposed to be served at such event;
(5) The names, addresses and alcoholic beverages license numbers of all persons purposing to sell alcoholic beverages at such event;
(6) The number of persons expected to attend the event;
(7) Any security arrangements to be provided by the person responsible for the staging of the proposed event;
(8) Any parking arrangements to be provided by the person responsible for the staging of the proposed event; and
(9) A sworn statement that the facts contained within said application are true and correct to the best of the applicant's knowledge, information and belief.
(d) Every person making such application for such a permit shall file the application with the clerk, and within two business days thereafter shall furnish and deliver to the chief of police a complete copy of said application. (e) In passing upon such applications, city council shall consider the following criteria:
(1) The public or quasi public nature of the proposed event, including, but not limited to, any economic impact or impact on tourism and/or commerce in the city.
(2) The impact of such event upon traffic and traffic safety within the city.
(3) The impact of such event upon fire safety in the city.
(4) The impact of such event upon public safety in general.
(5) The location of the proposed event.
(6) The adequacy of any proposed security and parking plans.
(7) Any past record or experiences of the proposed event in the city.
(8) The nature and quantity of the alcoholic beverages proposed to be served at the proposed event.
(9) The comment or comments, if any, of the chief of police.
(10) Whether or not the event will be catered.

578: The offense of loitering or prowling in the city is hereby declared unlawful. A person commits the offense of loitering or prowling when he is in a place at a time or in a manner not usual for law-abiding individuals under circumstances that warrant a justifiable and reasonable alarm or immediate concern for the safety of persons or property in the vicinity. Among the circumstances that may be considered in determining whether alarm is warranted is the fact that the person takes flight upon the appearance of a law enforcement officer, refuses to identify himself, or manifestly endeavors to conceal himself or any object. Unless flight by the person or other circumstances make it impracticable, a law enforcement officer shall, prior to any arrest for this offense, afford the person an opportunity to dispel any alarm or immediate concern that would otherwise be warranted by requesting the person to identify himself and explain his presence and conduct. No person shall be convicted of this offense if the law enforcement officer failed to comply with the foregoing procedure or if it appears at trial that the explanation given by the person was true and would have dispelled the alarm or immediate concern.

580:
(a) Fine established. To discourage excessive false alarms at any residential, commercial, institutional or educational location, enhance the safety of officers of the City of Richmond Hill Police and Fire Departments, protect the lives and property of the citizens and residents of the city, reduce unnecessary use of police and fire department resources, and produce revenues to defray costs of police and fire department responses to false alarms, a false alarm fine is hereby established.
(b) Definitions.
(1) Alarm system means an assembly of equipment and devices arranged to signal the presence of a hazard requiring urgent attention by the city police and/or fire department.
(2) False alarm means a bell, mechanical, electrical, or telephone apparatus, or combination thereof which is activated for the purpose of summoning the city police and/or fire department to respond to a hold-up, break-in, burglary, unauthorized entry, fire, destruction of property, or other event requiring police and/or fire department resources when in fact the service called for is not needed.
(3) Police officer means any sworn member of the city police department, Bryan County Sheriff's Department, or state law enforcement agency.
(4) Premises means any structure or other improvement to real property or any portion of any such structure or other improvement which is intended for separate use and occupancy apart from other portions thereof.
(5) Response means the dispatch of a police officer or fireman to the premises where an alarm system has been activated.
(6) Responsible person means any individual who owns, leases, manages, or otherwise controls such premises, whether such ownership, leasing, management, or control is shared with other persons and whether it is direct or indirect.
(7) Transmit means to send either manually or automatically, by any device or method, a signal to request a response or assistance from a police officer.
(8) Alarm user, with respect to any premises, means any individual who owns, leases, manages, or otherwise controls such premises, whether such ownership, leasing, management, or control is shared with other persons and whether it is direct or indirect.
(9) False alarm penalty means a fine imposed by the city to defray the expense to the city for responding to false alarms.
(10) Rate and base means the owner, lessee, or manager of any residential, commercial, institutional or educational property with an alarm system shall pay to the City of Richmond Hill a false alarm fine, based upon the total number of false alarms occurring at such location during the preceding 12 months. The 12-month period shall commence on January 1 and end on December 31 of any given year. The false alarm fine shall be charged as shown in the following schedule:
Number of False Alarms Within 12-Month Period | Fine
1—5 | No Charge
6—15 | $90.00, minimum
16—30 | 210.00, minimum
31—50 | 390.00, minimum
51 or more | 750.00 minimum
The maximum total of any and all fines during a designated 12 month period will not exceed $2,000.00. All false alarms will be calculated at the end of each year and the fine accessed accordingly.
(c) Grace period following installation of new alarm system. There shall be a 60-day grace period following the installation of any new alarm system during which period false alarms shall not be counted. This grace period is provided to allow the installing company or other installer and the user to take necessary corrective action with regard to the operation of the alarm system.
(d) Alarm systems to be installed with uninterrupted power supply or alternate power source. All alarm systems after the effective date of this ordinance must be equipped with an uninterrupted power supply or alternate power source capable of powering the alarm for a minimum of two hours in the event of a failure of the primary power supply.
(e) Registration of alarm systems with chief of police or his designee.
(1) Within ten working days after the installation or use of an alarm system, the person or business maintaining such alarm system shall register such alarm system with the chief of police or his designee on forms provided by the police department. Such registration information shall include, but not be limited to:
(2) The person or business maintaining the alarm system.
(3) The street address of the location of the alarm system.
(4) The make and model of the alarm system.
(5) The location of each alarm system within the building or structure and how it is activated.
(6) The person or business entity servicing the alarm system along with a telephone number of the alarm dispatch center.
(7) The name, address and telephone number of the person to be contacted in the event of an activation of the alarm system. (Key Holder)
(8) Persons or businesses maintaining existing alarm systems shall have 60 days from the effective date of this section to comply with the registration requirements set forth above.
(9) Registration is for business and educational facilities only. Residential premises are exempt from all registration requirements. All business and educational facilities, regardless of whether or not there is an existing alarm system are required to register. There will be a $4.00 registration fee payable to the police department at which point an alarm registration number will be issued. A decal with the designated number will be issued and must be posted within four feet of the front door of the alarmed premises. Failure to display the decal will result in a $25.00 fine being imposed.
(f) Notification of change of keyholder. The owner, lessee, or manager of any alarmed premise is responsible for notification of any change of the key holder. Said person must notify the police chief of any changes to include phone numbers in writing.
(g) Maintenance and operation. The responsible person of any residential, commercial, institutional or educational property with an alarm system shall (1) maintain the premises and alarm system in a manner that will minimize or eliminate false alarms, and (2) respond or cause their representative to appear at the alarm location within a reasonable period of time when notified by the city police and/or fire department or monitoring company to provide access to the premises, deactivate the alarm system, or provide security at the alarm location.
(h) Failure to terminate false alarm. Any responsible person of an alarmed premise failing to respond to the alarm location when requested to do so by the police department in order to reset, disconnect or disable the alarm system within 30 minutes of such request, shall be summoned to municipal court by a police officer. Those persons residing a considerable distance outside of the city limits will be afforded an appropriate amount of additional response time.
(i) Unlawful activation; failure to notify police department of malfunction or repair work. It is unlawful for anyone to activate any fire, robbery or burglar alarm for the purpose of summoning police officers except in the event of an actual fire, attempted burglary or robbery or for anyone notifying a police officer of an activated alarm and having knowledge that such activation was apparently caused by an electrical or other malfunction of the alarm system, or was apparently caused by maintenance or service to the alarm system, to fail at the same time to notify the police department of such apparent malfunction or repair.
(j) Shut off requirement. All audible alarm systems shall be equipped with shut-off devices that automatically silence the audible signal ten minutes after the alarm is initially activated except those systems required by law to have a longer period of activation, in which case such systems shall be so equipped so as to automatically shut off the audible signal at the conclusion of the longer time. Owners of alarm systems existing on or before the effective date of this ordinance shall have 60 days from the effective date to comply with the requirements set forth.
(k) Maximum decibel level. No alarm system which is installed on residentially zoned property or that is installed within 500 feet of a residentially zoned property, shall be allowed to emit sounds at levels greater than 95 decibels when measured at a distance of ten feet from the source of the emission.
(l) Penalties for violations of this section. Any person violating or failing to comply with any of the provisions of this section shall be summoned to the municipal court for each violation and/or noncompliance and, upon conviction, shall be punished as provided by law through the municipal court system.
(m) Notification of a false alarm. Following a false alarm at any residential, commercial, institutional or educational property, the city police and/or fire department shall notify the responsible person of said false alarm and the false alarm service fee due hereunder. Said notice shall be given by mailing a copy of the notice of false alarm prescribed by the city police and/or fire department to the alarmed premises, or by leaving a copy of said notice of false alarm at the alarmed premises.
(n) Exceptions. Each of the following circumstances shall not constitute a false alarm and no fine shall be assessed:
(1) Alarm conditions activated by a person working on the alarm system with prior notification to the city police and/or fire department.
(2) Alarms which can be substantiated as being activated by documented electrical interruptions, floods, or other natural disasters.
(3) Alarms which are activated as a result of an actual burglary, robbery, or fire.
(Ord. of 9-16-97, § 1)
Cross reference— False alarm, § 38-2.

City is the City of Richmond Hill.

Guardian is any person other than a parent, who has legal guardianship of a minor.

d. When the minor is attending or traveling directly to or from an activity involving the exercise of first amendment rights of speech, freedom of assembly or free exercise of religion;
e. When the minor is in a motor vehicle with parental consent for normal travel, with interstate travel through the city being excepted in all cases from the curfew.

(1) Any minor who has not attained the age of 16 violating the provisions of this section shall be dealt with in accordance with the juvenile court law and procedure. Any parent, guardian, or other adult person having the care and custody of a minor violating this section shall, after having been previously notified under subsection (c) of this section, be fined not more than $300.00 dollars for each offense.

591:

The tax imposed by this article shall be paid upon any occupancy on and after May 1, 2006, although such occupancy is had pursuant to a contract, lease or other arrangement made prior to such date.
(b) [The proceeds of said tax shall be used as follows:]
(1) An amount equal to 28.58 percent of the total taxes collected shall be deposited into a special account and kept segregated from all other city funds and expended, subject to the budgetary process, only for the purpose of operating, maintaining and marketing the Richmond Hill City Center, specifically including, but not limited to, servicing all debt incurred in the building, acquisition and construction of the center.
(2) An amount equal to 28.58 percent of the total taxes collected shall be deposited into a special account and kept segregated from all other city funds and expended, subject to the budgetary process, only for the following purposes:
i. Promoting tourism, conventions and trade shows;
ii. Supporting a facility owned or operated by a state authority for convention and trade show purposes or any other similar or related purposes;
iii. Supporting a facility owned or operated by the city or a local authority of the city for convention and trade show purposes or any other similar or related purposes; or
iv. Some combination of such purposes.
All of these amounts shall be expended only through a contract or contracts with the state, a department of state government, a state authority, the Richmond Hill Convention and Visitors Bureau Authority or a private sector, non-profit organization or through a contract or contracts with some combination of such entities, as council may from time to time approve, except that amounts expended for purpose (iii) may be expended in any lawful manner as council may from time to time approve.
(Ord. of 7-20-76, § 3; Ord. of 3-21-06; Ord. of 1-4-11, § I)
592:
Every operator maintaining a place of business in this city as provided in section 62-34, and renting guest rooms in this city, not exempted under section 62-36, shall collect a tax of seven percent on the amount of rent from the occupant.
(Ord. of 7-20-76, § 4; Ord. of 7-6-88, § 1; Ord. of 3-21-06)
593:
No tax shall be imposed under this article:
(1) Upon a permanent resident.
(2) Upon the rental or lease of any rooms, lodgings or accommodations furnished for a period of more than ten consecutive days.
(3) Upon the furnishing of rooms or accommodations for use as meeting rooms.
(4) For the use of state or local government officials or employees while traveling on official business for a period of more than one day. Whenever any person pays for any rooms, lodgings or accommodations with a state or local government credit or debit card, such rooms, lodgings or accommodations shall be deemed to have been furnished for use by such an official in such a capacity and subject to the exemption provided by this subparagraph.
(Ord. of 7-20-76, § 5; Ord. of 3-21-06)
594:
Every person engaging or about to engage in business as an operator of a hotel in this city shall immediately register with the city clerk on a form provided by the clerk. Persons engaged in such business must so register not later than 30 days after the date of the ordinance from which this section derives and the tax is imposed as set forth in section 62-33; but such privilege of registration after the imposition of such tax shall not relieve any person from the obligation of payment or collection of tax on and after the date of imposition thereof, regardless of registration. Such registration shall set forth the name under which such person transacts business or intends to transact business, the location of his place or places of business and such other information that would facilitate the collection of the tax as the clerk may require. The registration shall be signed by the owner if a natural person; in case of ownership by an association or partnership, by a member or partner; in the case of ownership by a corporation, by an officer. The city clerk shall, after such registration, issue without charge a certificate of authority to each operator to collect the tax from the occupant. A separate registration shall be required for each place of business of an operator. Each certificate shall state the name and location of the business to which it is applicable.
(Ord. of 7-20-76, § 6; Ord. of 7-20-99; Ord. of 3-21-06)
595:
(a) Due date of taxes. All amount of taxes shall be due and payable to the clerk monthly on or before the twentieth day of each month next succeeding each respective monthly period as set forth in section 62-31. Postage cancellation mark of the twentieth will be accepted.
(b) Return; time of filing; persons required to file; contents. On or before the 20th day of the month following each monthly period, a return for the preceding monthly period shall be filed with the city clerk showing the gross rent, rent from permanent residents, taxable rent, amount of tax collected or otherwise due for the related period, and such other information as may be required by the city clerk.
(c) Collection fee allowed operators. Operators collecting the tax shall be allowed a percentage of the tax due and accounted for and shall be reimbursed in the form of a deduction in submitting, reporting and payment of the amount due if the amount is not delinquent at the time of payment. The rate of the deduction shall be the same rate authorized for deduction from state tax under the Georgia Retailers and Consumers Sales and Use Tax Act, approved February 20, 1951, 1951 Ga. Laws, page 360, and now or hereafter amended.
(Ord. of 7-20-76, § 7; Ord. of 3-21-06)
596:
(a) Recomputation of tax; authority to make; basis of recomputation. If the city clerk is not satisfied with the return of the tax or the amount of tax required to be paid the city by any person, he/she may compute and determine the amount required to be paid upon the basis of any information in his/her possession or that may come into his/her possession. One or more deficiency determinations may be made of the amount due for one or more monthly periods.
(b) Interest on deficiency. The amount of the determination shall bear interest at the rate of one percent per month, or fraction thereof from the due date of taxes.
(c) Notice of determination; service of. The city clerk or his designated representatives shall give to the operator written notice of his determination. The notice may be served personally or by mail; if by mail such service shall be addressed to the operator at his address as it appears in the records of the city clerk. Service by mail is complete when delivered by certified mail with a receipt signed by the addressee.
(d) Time within which notice of deficiency determination to be mailed. Except in the case of failure to make a return, every notice of a deficiency determination shall be mailed within three years after the 20th day of the calendar month following the monthly period for which the amount is proposed to be determined, or within three years after the return is filed, whichever period shall last expire.
(Ord. of 7-20-76, § 8; Ord. of 3-21-06)
597:
(a) Estimate of gross receipts. If any person fails to make a return, the clerk shall make an estimate of the amount of the gross receipts of the person, or as the case may be, of the amount of the total rentals in this city that are subject to the tax. The estimate shall be made for the period in respect to which the person failed to make the return and shall be based upon any information that is or may come into the possession of the city clerk. Written notice shall be given in the manner prescribed in section 62-39(c).
(b) Interest on amount found due. The amount of the determination shall bear interest at the rate of one percent per month, or fraction thereof, from the 20th day of the month following the monthly period, for which the amount or any portion thereof should have been returned, until the date of payment.
(Ord. of 7-20-76, § 9; Ord. of 3-21-06)
598:
(a) Authority of city clerk. The city clerk shall administer and enforce the provisions of this article for the collection of the tax imposed by this article.
(b) Records required from operators, form. Every operator renting guest rooms in this city to a person shall keep such records, receipts, invoices and other pertinent papers in such form as the city clerk may require.
(c) Examination of records; audits. The city clerk or any person authorized in writing by the city clerk may examine the books, papers, records, financial reports, equipment and other facilities of any operator renting guest rooms to a person or any operator liable for the tax, in order to verify the accuracy of any return made, or if no return is made by the operator, to ascertain and determine the amount required to be paid.
(d) Authority to require reports; contents. In the administration of the provisions of this article, the city clerk may require the filing of reports by any person or class of persons having in such person's possession or custody information relating to rentals of guest rooms subject to the tax. The reports shall be filed with the city clerk when required and shall set forth the rental charged for each occupancy, the date of occupancy, and such other information as the city clerk may require.
(e) The city clerk may, for good cause, extend the time for making any returns required under this article for not more than 30 days. No extension shall be valid unless applied for and granted in writing. The extension shall only be valid for a period, as appropriate, of not more than 12 months or four consecutive calendar quarters. Upon the grant of an extension, the operator shall remit to the city clerk on or before the date the tax would otherwise become due without the grant of the extension an amount which equals not less than 100 percent of the operator's payment for the corresponding period of the preceding year. No interest or penalty shall be charged by reason of the granting of an extension pursuant to this paragraph during the first ten days of each extension period. Thereafter, interest shall be collected upon the unpaid balance of the operator's liability at the rate specified in section 62-39.
(Ord. of 7-20-76, § 12; Ord. of 3-21-06)
599:
(a) Action for tax; time for. At any time within three years after any tax or any amount of tax required to be collected becomes due and payable and at any time within three years after the delinquency of any tax or any amount of tax required to be collected, the city clerk may bring action in a court of competent jurisdiction in the name of the city to collect the amount delinquent, together with interest, court fees, filing fees, attorney's fees and other legal fees incident thereto.
(b) Duty of successors or assignees of operator to withhold tax from purchase money. If any operator liable for any amount under this article sells out his business or quits the business, his successors or assigns shall withhold sufficient of the purchase price to cover such amount until the former owner produces a receipt from the city clerk showing that he has been paid or a certificate stating that no amount is due.
(c) Liability for failure to withhold; certificate of notice of amount due; time to enforce successor's liability. If the purchaser of a business fails to withhold the purchase price as required, he shall be personally liable for the payment of the amount required to be withheld by him to the extent of the purchase price.
(d) Tax credit or interest paid more than once or erroneously or illegally collected. Whenever the amount of any tax or interest has been paid more than once, or has been erroneously or illegally collected or received by the city under this article, it may be offset by the city clerk. If the operator or person determines that he has overpaid or paid more than once, which fact has not been determined by the city clerk, he will have three years from date of payment to file claim in writing stating the specific ground upon which such claim is founded. The claim shall be audited. If the claim is approved by the city clerk, the excess amount paid the city may be credited on any amounts then due and payable from the person by whom it was paid, or his administrators or executors.
(Ord. of 3-21-06)

616:
The purpose of this chapter is to establish general guidelines for the siting of towers and antennas. The goals of this chapter are to:
(1) Encourage the location of towers in nonresidential areas and minimize the total number of towers throughout the community,
(2) Encourage strongly the joint use of new and existing tower sites,
(3) Encourage users of towers and antennas to locate them, to the extent possible, in areas where the adverse impact on the community is minimal,
(4) Encourage users of towers and antennas to configure them in a way that minimizes the adverse visual impact of the towers and antennas,
(5) Enhance the ability of the providers of telecommunications services to provide such services to the community quickly, effectively, and efficiently,
(6) Promote telecommunications facility safety through proper engineering and siting, and
(7) Encourage towers and antennas to be located at a height above the tree line no greater than necessary to reasonably accommodate the facility.
(Ord. of 1-16-98, § 1)
617:
As used in this chapter, the following terms shall have the meanings indicated:
Alternative tower structure shall mean the following man-made structures: bell towers, church steeples, light poles, water towers, utility structures, flag poles, existing telecommunications facilities, warehouses, factories, commercial buildings, billboards, publicly-used structures such as police and fire stations, courthouses, churches, schools, and similar alternative-design mounting structures that camouflage or conceal the presence of antennas or towers.
Antenna shall mean any exterior apparatus designed for telephonic, radio, or television communications through the sending and/or receiving of electromagnetic waves.
Building and zoning department shall mean the Building and Zoning Department of the City of Richmond Hill.
Commercial wireless telecommunication facility shall mean antennas and/or towers, either individually or together, used for the purpose of facilitating one or more applications of a broad range of spectrum-based commercial wireless services. Such services are provided by wireless communications carriers to one or more subscriber(s) for a profit. These services include: one-way and two-way voice and data communications, data messaging, wireless modems, e-mail, voice mail, conference calling, dispatching, paging and facsimile.
FAA shall mean the Federal Aviation Administration.
FCC shall mean the Federal Communications Commission.
Governing authority shall mean the governing authority of the City of Richmond Hill.
Guyed tower shall mean a telecommunications tower that is supported, in whole or in part, by guy wires and ground anchors.
Height shall mean, when referring to a tower or other structure, the vertical distance measured from ground level to the highest point on the tower or other structure, even if said highest point is an antenna.
Lattice tower shall mean a telecommunications tower that has open-framed supports on three or four sides and is constructed without guy wires or ground anchors.
Monopole tower shall mean a telecommunications tower constructed of a single pole, without guy wires or ground anchors.
City planning commission shall mean the City Planning Commission of the City of Richmond Hill.
Preexisting towers and antennas shall have the meaning set forth in this section above. (See "commercial wireless telecommunication facility.")
Provider shall mean any carrier or provider of commercial wireless telecommunications services that are subscriber based for profit.
Public use shall mean any buildings, structures and uses of land owned, operated and maintained by a government agency, including, but not restricted to, public schools, fire stations, recreation-sites and facilities and water treatment facilities.
Stealth shall mean the concealing, camouflaging, or designing of wireless antennas or attachments to have the appearance of being part of the structure or building facade or exterior.
Tower shall mean any vertical structure that is designed and constructed primarily for the purpose of supporting one or more antennas for the purpose of transmitting or receiving telecommunications as authorized by the FCC, including self-supporting lattice towers, guy towers, or monopole towers. The term includes radio and television transmission towers, microwave towers, common carrier towers, cellular telephone towers, alternative tower structures, and the like.
Tower farm shall mean multiple towers on a single site.
(Ord. of 1-16-98, § 2)
618:
Telecommunications facilities are conditionally permitted only within the Light Industrial, General Industrial, Flood Hazard, and Interchange Commercial districts. Buildings and other supporting equipment used in conjunction with the telecommunication facility are also permitted. (Ord. of 1-16-98, § 3)
619:
The following telecommunications facilities are exempted from the requirements of this chapter, except as stated below:
(1) Public property exemption. Antennas or towers located on property owned, leased, or otherwise controlled by the governing authority shall be exempt from the requirements of this chapter, provided a license or lease authorizing such antenna or tower has been approved by the governing authority and the applicant provides all of the information required in section 63-6(a) of this chapter.
(2) Amateur radio and receive-only antennas. This chapter shall not govern any tower, or the installation of any antenna, that is under seventy (70) feet in height and is owned and operated by a federally-licensed amateur radio station operator or is used exclusively for receive only antennas.
(3) Pre-existing towers and antennas. Any tower or antenna for which a permit has been properly issued prior to the effective date of this chapter shall not be required to meet the requirements of this chapter, other than the requirements of sections 63-5(g) and (h). Any such towers or antennas shall be referred to in this chapter as "preexisting towers or preexisting antennas."
(Ord. of 1-16-98, § 4)
620:
The guidelines set forth in section 63-3 and this section shall govern the location of all towers, and the installation of all antennas, governed by this chapter; provided, however, that the governing authority may waive these requirements if it determines that the goals of this chapter are better served thereby. The city council shall, in making such decision, consider the criteria contained at section 63-6(b) and section 63-7 of this chapter.
(1) Setbacks and separation. The following setbacks and separation requirements shall apply to all towers and antennas for which a conditional permitted use is required; provided, however, that the governing authority may, reduce the standard setbacks and separation requirements if the goals of this chapter would be better served thereby. The city council shall, in making such decision, consider the criteria contained at section 63-6(b) and section 63-7 of this chapter.
a. Towers must be set back a minimum distance of 100 feet or a distance equal to the height of the tower, whichever is greater, from any off-site residential structure.
b. Towers, guys, and accessory facilities must satisfy the minimum zoning district setback requirements.
c. Towers shall not be located within one-quarter of a mile from any existing tower, except within tower farms.
d. Telecommunications towers shall be set back not less than 30 feet from any property line adjacent to a right-of-way or approved access easement and not less than thirty (30) feet from any existing building.
(2) Antenna on existing structure. It is permitted to install an antenna on an existing structure other than a tower (such as a building, sign, light pole, water tower, or other freestanding nonresidential structure) that is 50 feet in height or greater, so long as said additional antenna adds no more than 20 feet to the height of said existing structure.
(3) Antenna on existing tower. It is permitted to install an antenna on any existing tower of any height, so long as the addition of said antenna adds no more than twenty (20) feet to the height of said existing tower and said existing tower is not a preexisting tower; provided, however, that such specific permitted use shall not include the placement of additional buildings or other supporting equipment used in connection with said antenna.
(4) Principal or accessory use. Antennas and towers may be considered either principal or accessory uses. A different existing use or an existing structure on the same lot shall not preclude the installation of an antenna or tower on such lot. For purposes of determining whether the installation of a tower or antenna complies with district development regulations, including but not limited to set-back requirements, lot-coverage requirements, and other such requirements, the dimensions of the entire lot shall control, even though the antennas or towers may be located on leased parcels within such lots. Towers that are constructed and antennas that are installed in accordance with the provisions of this chapter shall not be deemed to constitute the expansion of a nonconforming use or structure.
(5) Inventory of existing sites. Each applicant for an antenna and or tower shall provide to the building and zoning department an inventory of its existing towers that are either within the jurisdiction of the governing authority or within one quarter mile of the border thereof, including specific information about the location, height, and design of each tower. The building and zoning department may share such information with other applicants applying for conditional permitted use permits under this chapter or other organizations seeking to locate antennas within the jurisdiction of the governing authority, provided, however that the building and zoning department is not, by sharing such information, in any way representing or warranting that such sites are available or suitable.
(6) Aesthetics; lighting. The requirements set forth in this Section shall govern the aesthetics and lighting for telecommunications facilities.
a. Towers shall either maintain a galvanized steel finish or, subject to any applicable standards of the FAA, be painted a neutral color, so as to reduce visual obtrusiveness.
b. At a tower site, the design of the buildings and related structures shall, to the extent possible, use materials, colors, textures, screening, and landscaping that will blend the tower facilities to the natural setting and built environment.
c. If an antenna is installed on a structure other than a tower, the antenna and supporting electrical and mechanical equipment must be of a neutral color that is identical to, or closely compatible with, the color of the supporting structure so as to make the antenna and related equipment as visually unobtrusive as possible.
d. Towers shall not be artificially lighted, unless required by the FAA or other applicable authority. If lighting is required, the governing authority may review the available lighting alternatives and approve the design that would cause the least disturbance to the surrounding views. The city council shall, in making such decision, consider the criteria contained at section 63-6(b) and section 63-7 of this chapter.
e. Except for the manufacturer's name plate, advertising on telecommunications facilities shall be prohibited.
(7) Federal requirements. All towers must meet or exceed current standards and regulations of the FAA, the FCC, and any other agency of the federal government with the authority to regulate towers and antennas. If such standards and regulations are changed, then the owners of the towers and antennas governed by this chapter shall bring such towers and antennas into compliance with such revised standards and regulations within six months of the effective date of such standards and regulations, unless a more stringent compliance schedule is mandated by the controlling federal agency. Failure to bring towers and antennas into compliance with such revised standards and regulations shall constitute grounds for the removal of the tower or antenna at the owner's expense. Any such removal by the governing authority shall be in the manner provided in Sections 41-2-8 through 41-2-17 of the Official Code of Georgia.
(8) Building codes; safety standards. To ensure the structural integrity of towers, the owner of a tower shall ensure that it is maintained in compliance with standards contained in applicable local building codes and the applicable standards for towers that are published by the Electronic Industries Association and the American National Standards Institute (ANSI), as amended from time to time. If, upon inspection, the governing authority concludes that a tower fails to comply with such codes and standards and constitutes a danger to persons or property, then upon notice being provided to the owner of the tower, the owner shall have 30 days to bring such tower into compliance with such standards. If the owner fails to bring such tower into compliance within said 30 days, the governing authority may remove such tower at the owner's expense. Any such removal by the governing authority shall be in the manner provided in Sections 41-2-8 through 41-2-17 of the Official Code of Georgia.
(9) Access. Access for maintenance vehicles shall be via collector, arterial right-of-way, approved access easements, or other access as approved by the City Planning Commission.
(10) Accessory structures. Accessory structures shall be used only to house equipment and other supplies in support of the tower operation. Such structures shall not be used for offices. Any equipment not used in direct support of tower operation shall not be stored on-site.
(11) Historic sites telecommunications facilities. Historic sites telecommunications facilities shall not be attached to or mounted to historically significant buildings or structures.
(12) Security fencing. Towers shall be enclosed by security fencing not less than six feet in height and shall also be equipped with an appropriate anti-climbing device: provided, however, that the governing authority may waive such requirements, as it deems appropriate. The city council shall, in making such decision, consider the criteria contained at section 63-6(b) and section 63-7 of this chapter.
(13) Landscaping. The following requirements shall govern the landscaping surrounding towers for which a conditional permitted use permit is required; provided, however, that the governing authority may waive such requirements if the goals of this chapter would be better served thereby. The city council shall, in making such decision, consider the criteria contained at section 63-6(b) and section 63-7 of this chapter.
a. Tower facilities shall be landscaped with a buffer of plant materials that effectively screens the view of the tower compound from adjacent property. The standard buffer shall consist of a landscaped strip at least ten feet wide outside the perimeter of the compound. This buffer requirement applies to both owned or leased land.
b. In locations where the visual impact of the tower would be minimal, the landscaping requirement may be reduced or waived altogether. The city council shall, in making such decision, consider the criteria contained in section 63-6(b) and section 63-7 of this chapter.
c. Within three years, landscaping will produce a 90 percent screen of the base of the tower, the security fence, and any telecommunications facility building(s). Existing mature tree growth and natural land forms on the site shall be preserved to the maximum extent possible; however, the 90 percent screen within three years requirement still applies. This could be met by adding evergreens to the mature tree growth already in place. In some cases, such as towers sited on large, wooded lots, natural growth around the property perimeter may be sufficient buffer; however, this shall be the case only if the landscape buffer is on telecommunication facility property and/or is protected by a tree easement. A tree survey of existing trees by a registered surveyor must be submitted for verification that existing trees are sufficient.
(Ord. of 1-16-98, § 5)
621:
(a) Application and fee. Application for a building permit for any telecommunications facility, including but not limited to towers, antennas or alternative tower structures, shall be made to the building and zoning department. The fee for a telecommunications facility application is $8.00 per thousand dollars ($1,000.00) of facility cost. Such applications will be scheduled for public hearing, followed by city planning commission review and recommendation, and then review and approval or disapproval by the mayor and city council of Richmond Hill depending on the criteria in sections 63-1 and 63-6(b) of this chapter. Incomplete applications shall not be considered. Applications will contain the following:
(1) A scaled site plan and a scaled elevation view and other supporting drawings, calculations, and other documentation, signed and sealed by appropriate licensed professionals, showing the location and dimensions of all improvements, including information concerning topography, radio frequency coverage, tower height requirements, setbacks, drives, parking, fencing, landscaping, adjacent uses, and other information deemed by the governing authority to be necessary to assess compliance with this chapter.
(2) An inventory of the applicant's existing telecommunications facilities as provided at section 63-5(5) of this chapter, including the specific location, height, and design of each tower.
(3) A description of the telecommunication facility's area of service.
(4) Proof of ownership of the proposed site or documentation that the applicant has authorization from the owner to utilize the proposed site.
(5) Photo simulations or renderings of the proposed telecommunications tower(s) illustrating the potential visual impact, as viewed from at least two places nearby (public places if possible). (All costs for visual analysis, and applicable administrative costs, shall be borne by the applicant.)
(6) A written statement of the general capacity of a proposed tower in terms of the number and type of antennas it is designed to accommodate.
(7) Evidence to demonstrate that no existing tower or structure can accommodate the applicant's antenna. Such evidence must consist of the following:
a. No existing towers or structures are located within the geographic area required to meet applicant's engineering requirements.
b. Existing towers or structures are not of sufficient height to meet applicant's engineering requirements.
c. Existing towers or structures do not have sufficient structural strength to support applicant's proposed antenna and related equipment.
d. The applicant's proposed antenna would cause electromagnetic interference with the antenna on the existing towers or structures, or the antenna on the existing towers or structures would cause interference with the applicant's proposed antenna.
e. The fees, costs, or contractual provisions required by the owner in order to share an existing tower or structure or to adapt an existing tower or structure for sharing are unreasonable. Costs exceeding new tower development are presumed to be unreasonable.
f. The applicant demonstrates that there are other limiting factors that render existing towers and structures unsuitable.
(b) Factors considered in granting conditional permitted use.
